newsitem.title: USA: SPIEGEL'S EDDIE BAUER JULY SAME STORE SALES SLIP.
newsitem.headline: SPIEGEL'S EDDIE BAUER JULY SAME STORE SALES SLIP.

text.p: Spiegel Inc said Thursday that comparable-store July sales for its Eddie Bauer subsidiary fell one percent for the four-week period ended July 26, 1997.
For the 30 weeks ended July 26, 1997, comparable Eddie Bauer store sales sales rose three percent on top of a two percent rise in the comparable period last year.
Total Spiegel sales for the four weeks ended July 26, 1997 rose seven percent to $161.8 million from $151.6 million in the same period last year, the company said in a news release.
For 30 weeks ended July 26, 1997, total Spiegel sales were $1.378 billion versus $1.365 billion in the year-ago period.

The company said that despite the United Parcel Service of America Inc strike, Spiegel Catalog and Eddie Bauer have continued to process and ship customers' orders, with catalog shipments delivered via the U.S. Postal Service (USPS). Its Newport News division ordinarily ships via USPS.
It said it will continue to monitor the situation and take the necessary steps to serve its customers.

Spiegel Inc. is an international, specialty retailer marketing fashionable apparel and home furnishings to customers through catalogs and more than 450 specialty retail stores. Spiegel's businesses include Spiegel Catalog, Eddie Bauer, Eddie Bauer HOME, AKA EDDIE BAUER, and Newport News. -- ((Reuters Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
